ALPHABET CENTER · LETTER S

Letter S — Snake.

The letters S s slither in with a green snake. S hisses — sss — and is written as one wiggly stroke, just like a snake path.

Meet the letter, hear its sound, trace it together — then play. Everything on this page is free, gentle and paced for you.

THE LETTER SOUND

What does S say?

“s — sss, a hissing sound”

S says sss — a long hiss like a snake in the grass. Make it long and silly: sssss. If it sounds like air escaping a tire, it is perfect.

TRACE THE LETTER

Trace S s together.

Follow the numbers with a finger — on screen or on each other’s palms. The arrows show the way to go, the numbers show where to start, and a grown-up reads the little script below each card. Slow and wobbly is exactly right.

Trace the uppercase S

One stroke. Start at 1 at the top right, curve round to the left like a little c, then slide right and curve back down and round to the bottom left.

Trace the lowercase s

One stroke. Start at 1 at the top right, curve round to the left, slide right, then curve back down and round to the bottom left.

TAKE IT OFF SCREEN

Snake trail.

Two minutes is plenty. Follow your child’s lead and stop while it is still fun — that is the whole method.

  1. 01

    Walk your fingers in a wiggly line across the floor, hissing ssss.

  2. 02

    Draw a giant S with chalk or on paper and walk a toy along the path.

  3. 03

    Curl up like a coiled snake — one gentle squeeze — then uncoil with a hiss.

PLAY & PRACTICE

Games that use this letter.

The games mix every letter — play them after meeting two or three letters, or any day your child asks. No scores, no timers, no wrong answers that count.
